purpose: Strengthen the sparse counterexample so even interpreting the overloaded alpha literally as both smoothness and significance keeps alpha in(0,1). Original report remains intact; SOLIT counterexample unchanged.
all_hypotheses: All positivity, q, Countable Choice, nonempty sequence alternative, nonempty relaxed feasible set and delta conditions are checked exactly as in the original report. Now alpha also lies in(0,1), so the contradiction is independent of the notation defect.
proof: The relaxed constraints are E=sum_j j h_j z_j^2≥r_tilde^2/epsilon^2 and Bq=sum_j j^(3/2)h_j z_j^(3/2)≤epsilon^(-3/2). Let W=sum_j h_j^2 sinh^2(z_j^2/2).
On z_j≤Tj, j h_j z_j^2≤T^(1/2)j^(3/2)h_j z_j^(3/2); these indices carry energy≤r_tilde^2/(2epsilon^2). The complementary set carries at least the same half-energy.

Cauchy-Schwarz on the complementary set gives E_H^2≤W F_H, with F_H=sum_H j^2 z_j^4/sinh^2(z_j^2/2). For T≥2, monotonicity of z^4/sinh^2(z^2/2) gives F_H≤16T^4 sum_j j^6 exp(-T^2 j^2)≤C0 T^4 exp(-T^2). The finite C0 follows from j^6≤6!binom(j+5,6) and exp[-T^2(j^2-1)]≤exp[-(j-1)].
Taking the infimum gives u_epsilon^2≥r_tilde^4 exp(T^2)/(2 C0 epsilon^4 T^4), growing faster than every fixed power because T^2~epsilon^(-1)/16.
The claimed asymptotic now gives u_epsilon~c epsilon^(-A/D)r_epsilon^(B/D)=c epsilon^(-7/2)epsilon=c epsilon^(-5/2), contradiction.
